Concept Design · Buildable Prop / Recreation Device

NYLON ROPE “WEB SHOOTER”

Wrist-mounted line launcher — codename Spin-Drift Mk I

Spring-powered launch Motorized reel ≈25 m nylon line Blunt-tip dart August 2026 · v1.0 Safety-first design

1Overview

Spin-Drift Mk I is a wrist-mounted, spring-powered launcher that fires a blunt, magnet-tipped grappling dart trailing a high-strength braided nylon line, then reels the line back in with a small geared motor. It's an engineering homage to the comic-book web-shooter, designed as a real, buildable cosplay / recreation device — not a weapon and not a climbing rig.

Launch
Spring piston · ≈5 J
Retrieve
Motorized reel · ≈2 m/s
Reach
Up to ≈25 m

The design splits into four subsystems: a frame & mount, a line system (spool + bearings + nylon), a launch system (spring + piston + barrel + dart), and a rewind/power system (motor + clutch + LiPo). Everything is sized for home-shop tools and a 3D printer.

2How it works

Step 1 · Load
Line is pulled out and laid clean on the spool; spool free-spins on bearings so it pays out without tangling.
Step 2 · Fire
Squeeze the trigger → sear releases the piston → mainspring drives the dart out of the barrel, trailing the line.
Step 3 · Retract
Flick the thumb switch → geared motor spins the spool through a one-way clutch and reels the line home.

5Cost breakdown

6Build order

  1. Print / machine the housing in two shells (PETG or aluminum) and fit the wrist strap with foam padding.
  2. Assemble the line system — press the two bearings into the spool, mount it on its axle, and wind the 25 m nylon line under light tension.
  3. Fit the launch train — slide the mainspring and piston into the barrel, and mount the barrel along the top rail of the housing.
  4. Install the trigger group — sear hook, trigger bar, pivot pin, and the sliding safety lock; test that the sear catches and releases cleanly.
  5. Mount the rewind drive — N20 motor and one-way clutch, aligned so the clutch free-wheels when the line pays out and engages on retract.
  6. Wire the power — 2S LiPo, charge board, and a momentary thumb switch (or wrist-twist switch) to the motor.
  7. Route the line — from the spool, through the ceramic guide, to the dart eyelet; verify a snag-free payout.
  8. Test & tune — fire into a soft backstop at low tension first, adjust sear engagement and line drag, then work up to full range.

7Safety & legal

This is a low-power recreation device — build and use it responsibly.
  • Dart tip is blunt and rounded; launch energy is capped at ≈5 J (spring) so it will not penetrate skin. The CO₂ module (≈8 J) is for experienced builders only.
  • Never aim at people, animals, or faces. Wear eye protection; keep bystanders behind you.
  • Not rated for climbing, swinging, or suspending any load — the anchor and launch are not life-safety equipment, regardless of the line's 200 lb rating.
  • Check local laws before building or carrying — some areas regulate spring/CO₂ projectors and grappling-type launchers.
  • Store unloaded, safety engaged, and keep the CO₂ cartridge (if fitted) removed when not in use.

Treat the Spin-Drift Mk I the way you'd treat a low-power airsoft or slingshot device: supervised, aimed only at safe targets, and never used to secure or lift weight.
